title: Introduce kernel handshake layer to coordinate v2/v3 selection and prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight 'kernel handshake' abstraction in the serving runtime that negotiates which attention kernel variant (FlashAttention v2 or v3 or fallback) to use for a request before prefill starts and to coordinate a safe handoff at decode time. Goals: reduce kernel-flip induced tail latency regressions, avoid workspace thrash/evictions during bursts, and provide observability + safe rollout controls.
background: In recent integration tests we observed increased P95/P99 decode tail latency and intermittent OOMs when the runtime switched kernel variants mid-request for mixed workloads (short and long contexts, mixed quantization). Root causes: (1) workspace allocation churn when switching kernels during decode, (2) eviction of prefill-cached KV state when memory planners rebind buffers to different microkernels, (3) increased scheduling jitter as kernel selector triggers probing under bursty traffic. Existing mitigations (static per-model pinning) are too coarse for multi-tenant bursty workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Handshake layer negotiates kernel choice before prefill and guarantees no kernel swap during a single request unless explicitly allowed by policy.
P95 and P99 decode latency regression compared to baseline reduced to within +5ms of current stable runtime across representative workloads (chat short/long, streaming, embeddings-heavy).
No increase in OOM incidents on canary fleet during 72h continuous synthetic workload replay.
Instrumentation surfaces per-request kernel decision reason and probe events; dashboards added to runtime-1.20 release board.
Canary rollout automation with 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% ramps and automated rollback triggers configured.
plan: Design handshake API: request context includes model variant, quantization, shape fingerprint, latency budget, and cache-warmness hint.
Implement KernelHandshake module that returns (kernel_variant, safety_token) and reserves 'slot' allocations for the chosen kernel for the request lifetime.
Add prefill-time enforcement: prefill allocates workspace based on handshake decision; if allocation fails, fallback policy selects compatible variant or queues request.

Add decode-time guard: if runtime discovers a mismatch between handshake decision and current kernel availability, it either proceeds with graceful fallback (compatibility shim) or aborts with clear telemetry tag.
Create synthetic replay harness reproducing mixed traffic shapes and quantization permutations for stress testing.
Add telemetry: per-request kernel_choice, decision_reason, probe_latency, workspace_allocations, memory_rebind_count.
Run internal benchmarks on A100/H100 and on small GPU instances (T4) to validate multi-arch behaviour.
Prepare canary run with escalation/rollback policy and alert thresholds for latency and OOMs.
Document API and rollout playbook in Confluence and link PRs and dashboards.
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Spike finished — prototype handshake API defined; validated simple decision logic (shape+quant->kernel) in unit harness.
2026-03-02: Microbenchmark results: for batch=1, seq=128 on H100: v3 decode P50=6.2ms, P95=9.7ms; v2 decode P50=6.8ms, P95=10.2ms — differences small but v3 uses ~12% more workspace in this config.

2026-03-05: Reproducer found: mid-request kernel swap triggers rebind path that frees and re-allocates KV workspace, causing +20–40ms tail spikes in mixed-quant workloads. Recorded memory_rebind_count correlated with P99 spikes.
2026-03-07: Implemented kernel 'slot' reservation prototype — prefill reserves kernel-specific workspace early; synthetic replay shows reduced rebind_count by ~80% in the harness.
2026-03-10: Integrated basic telemetry tags into request trace: kernel_choice and decision_reason appear in traces and are linkable from Console traces page.
2026-03-13: Canary configuration draft ready; thresholds: P95 > baseline + 10ms OR OOM rate increase > 0.1% over baseline -> automatic rollback. Preparing PRs.
benchmarks_and_results: H100 (batch=1) chat-short (seq=64): baseline runtime-1.19 P95=8.6ms; handshake-enabled P95=8.9ms (+0.3ms).
H100 (batch=1) chat-long (seq=2048): baseline P95=120ms; handshake-enabled P95=118ms (-2ms), observed fewer P99 spikes.
A100 (batch=4) mixed-quant replay: handshake reduces memory_rebind_count from 17 -> 3 over a 30s burst; observed P99 reduction of ~28ms in the harness.
T4 (batch=8) embeddings workload: no measurable latency regression; handshake avoids a single reproducible OOM previously seen in v3 probing scenario.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Extra hop: handshake adds ~150–400us decision latency in the hot path; acceptable for most workloads but may impact extreme low-latency SLAs (we expose opt-out).
Resource reservation: slot reservations can reduce packing efficiency; will be mitigated by conservative reservation sizes and short reservation lifetimes for streaming workloads.
Complexity: additional state increases runtime surface area and testing burden. We will gate with canary and keep compatibility shims to reduce blast radius.
Fallback policy complexity: multiple fallback tiers (compatible memcpy shim, quantization-adjusted kernel) require careful validation to avoid correctness regressions.
review_feedback: PM (Rosa Nguyen): prefer conservative default to avoid latency regressions for hosted API customers; require opt-in aggressive probing per-customer.
SRE (Diego Morales): add explicit metrics for rebind_count, allocation_failures, and an OOM alert dashboard before canary ramp.
Security (Lena Okafor): handshake metadata contains model/shape hints — ensure no PII and scrub any prompt tokens in traces; KMS keys unaffected.
Perf (internal reviewer): request benchmarking harness to include sequence distribution matching production traces — currently synthetic skew may under/over-estimate impact.
decisions: Decision 1: Handshake will be executed at prefill start and will be treated as authoritative for that request; kernel swaps mid-request are disallowed unless explicit 'staged-handoff' policy is triggered.
Decision 2: Default policy: prefer v3 when sequence length > 512 OR model flagged as 'long-context-optimized'; otherwise prefer v2 for memory efficiency.
Decision 3: Expose per-tenant opt-in for experimental aggressive probing; default to conservative behavior for hosted customers.
Decision 4: Canary thresholds: P95 > baseline + 10ms OR P99 > baseline + 25ms OR OOMs increase > 0.1% triggers rollback.
canary_plan: Stage 0: internal cluster run (0% external traffic) for 48h with replay harness — validate no OOMs and telemetry correctness.
Stage 1: 1% external traffic for 24h with strict alerts enabled.
Stage 2: 5% for 24h, observe tail metrics and memory indicators.
Stage 3: 25% for 48h, then 100% if stable. Automated rollback on triggers.
attachments: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/1399 - Related repro issue for mid-request kernel swap
notes: This ticket aims to strike a balance between safety (no mid-request kernel swaps) and performance (allowing v3 benefits where appropriate). Keep the implementation minimal and observable; follow-on work may expand staged handoff and per-layer kernel decisions.
